en: (서울=연합뉴스) 윤보람 기자 = 조셉 윤 전 미국 국무부 대북정책특별대표는 미국 중간선거 결과에 따라 한미 간 전시작전통제권(전작권) 전환과 핵추진잠수함(핵잠) 도입에 제약이 커질 것으로 전망했다. 윤 전 대표는 7일 미국의소리(VOA) 방송과의 화상 인터뷰에서 중간선거 결과 민주당이 상·하원을 모두 장악한 데 따른 한미동맹 영향을 묻는 말에 이같이 답변했다. 그는 우선 "(확장억제와 같은) 한미동맹의 핵심 사안에 있어선 모든 핵심 가치를 준수하며 초당적인 접근을 하겠다는 행정부와 의회 양측의 약속이 존재한다"면서 큰 영향이 없을 것으로 예상했다. 그러나 전작권 전환과 핵잠 도입 같은 "새로운 이니셔티브 중 일부는 한쪽 또는 다른 쪽의 추진력 부족으로 인해 향후 2년 동안 별다른 진전이 없도록 보류될 수도 있다고 생각한다"며 "새로운 것을 추진하기에는 어려움이 따를 수도 있다고 본다"고 말했다. 대북정책과 관련해선 행정부의 권한이 크고 당장 북한에 대한 미국의 지원이 없는 만큼 의회가 영향을 미칠 여지는 작다고 짚었다. 다만 북미대화 성사 가능성에 대해선 "김정은 측의 열의 부족 때문에 (북미대화가) 일어나지 않았다"며 "이번 선거든 그 어떤 것이든 그 방정식을 바꾸지 않는다고 생각한다"고 평가했다. 그는 북러·북중 관계 개선을 비롯해 "모든 면에서 북한은 트럼프 1기 행정부 때보다 더 잘, 훨씬 더 잘 지내고 있다"면서 "전략적으로 그들은 미국 대통령을 다시 만나는 데서 아무런 이득도 보지 못한다"고 지적했다. 중간선거 결과와 무관하게 북미대화 성사의 열쇠를 쥔 김정은 국무위원장이 소극적이어서 대화 재개 가능성이 크지 않다고 본 것이다. 윤 전 대표는 한미 통상관계와 관련, 현재의 대외 통상정책과 관세정책은 계속될 것이라며 "의회는 우호국의 투자를 전폭적으로 지지한다"고 언급했다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/07 07:43 송고 2026년11월07일 07시43분 송고

Unlock these with Subscription India and the European Union have concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with a Euro 93.5 billion flagship research and innovation programme, paving the way for expanded collaboration under their broader strategic partnership. The decision comes weeks before India and the 27-nation bloc are set to seal a landmark free trade agreement — billed as the “mother of all deals” — to create a market of two billion people. The European Commission and India have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with the Horizon Europe programme, the EU said. This marks an important step forward for EU-India relations, strengthening scientific cooperation, creating new opportunities in research, and deepening the strategic partnership, it said. India’s association with the Horizon programme is seen as part of the comprehensive strategic agenda of the two sides for the next five years. For researchers, businesses and research organisations across Europe, India’s association will open up more opportunities to collaborate with Indian partners and build lasting scientific and technological links, the EU said. Once the agreement is signed and the necessary procedures are completed on both sides, researchers and organisations in India will be able to receive funding directly from Horizon Europe and lead collaborative projects under its Pillar II: ‘Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness’, it said. This is the largest part of the programme which funds collaborative, multi-national research and innovation projects tackling societal and technological issues, such as health, digital, industry, space, climate, energy, and bioeconomy. The EU said the move will create new opportunities for European and Indian partners to pool expertise, develop technologies and address shared challenges. Association is the closest form of cooperation offered by the EU to non-EU countries under Horizon Europe. It allows organisations in associated countries to participate on equal terms with their EU counterparts in the parts of the programme covered by the agreement. In return, associated countries contribute financially to the programme. The successful conclusion of negotiations clears the way for the signature of the association agreement, subject to the completion of the necessary procedures on both sides. The two sides are likely to sign the formal agreement in January. India and the EU had launched the exploratory discussions on the Horizon programme in February 2026, and formal negotiations began in July. EU-India scientific cooperation builds on the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation, signed in 2001 and renewed until 2030. Research and innovation also form an integral part of the Joint EU-India Comprehensive Strategic Agenda towards 2030, adopted at the summit talks between the two sides in New Delhi on January 27. The partnership has been strengthened through the EU-India Trade and Technology Council, which facilitates collaboration on key digital areas such as artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, semiconductors, high-performance computing, digital skills and the sixth generation of wireless telecommunications. The EU and India took a further step in collaboration on digital skills through the launch of the first-ever European Legal Gateway Office in India last February, aiming to facilitate safe, legal and well-informed mobility to the EU in the ICT sector. Horizon Europe runs from 2021 to 2027, with a budget of 93.5 billion euro. International cooperation is central to the programme, bringing together expertise and resources to advance scientific excellence and innovation. Currently, 23 non-EU countries are associated with Horizon Europe. They are Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Canada, Egypt, the Faroe Islands, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Japan, Korea, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Switzerland, Türkiye, Tunisia, Ukraine and the United Kingdom.
